title: Java Recursion
learningObjectives: Define recursion as a method calling itself directly or indirectly.
Identify a base case that stops recursive calls.
Explain how each recursive call should move toward the base case.
Trace a simple recursive method and its returned result.
Recognize stack growth and when an iterative solution may be safer.

understand.concept: Recursion is a problem-solving technique in which a method calls itself with a smaller or simpler input. A correct recursive method has a base case that returns without another recursive call and a recursive step that makes progress toward that base case.
understand.whyItMatters: Some problems naturally divide into smaller versions of themselves, such as factorial calculations and traversing nested structures. Understanding recursion also teaches how method calls use the call stack.
understand.analogy: Think of a method as a named tool: give it the information it needs, let it perform one defined task, and use its result when appropriate.
understand.analogyLimit: A program follows exact language rules; a real-world tool may need judgment and safety checks that code must model explicitly.

explain.narrative:
## Base case and recursive case

A recursive method needs a base case to stop. Its recursive case calls the method again with an input that moves closer to the base case. Without progress or a reachable base case, calls can continue until a `StackOverflowError` occurs.

## Trace the calls

Each call has its own parameter values and local variables. Calls return in reverse order: the deepest call returns first, then its caller continues.

## Recursion versus iteration

A loop can often solve the same problem without creating a new method call for every step. Recursion can make a naturally recursive problem easier to express, but very deep recursion can exhaust the call stack.

## Common mistakes

- Omitting the base case.
- Making a recursive call with an input that does not get closer to the base case.
- Using the wrong return expression when calls unwind.
- Assuming recursion is always more efficient than a loop.

examples.title: Countdown with a base case
examples.explanation: The base case at zero stops the sequence after each smaller call.

examples.title: Calculate factorial recursively
examples.explanation: Each call multiplies n by the factorial of the next smaller integer.

examples.title: Sum numbers recursively
examples.explanation: The base case contributes zero and the calls add 4, 3, 2 and 1.

examples.title: Find a power recursively
examples.explanation: Each call reduces the exponent until it reaches zero.

examples.title: Use recursion to print array values
examples.explanation: The index increases on each call and the base case stops at the array length.

practise.independentTask: Build an original program that uses java recursion to solve a practical task. Include at least two test cases, state their expected outputs, and verify them by compiling and running the program.
hints: Trace each statement and record the relevant variable values before predicting output.
Use descriptive names and braces so the program structure is easy to follow.

questions.explanation: A recursive method makes another call to itself.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a base case?
questions.explanation: The base case returns without making another recursive call.

questions.prompt: What should each recursive step do?
questions.answer: Move the input closer to the base case
options: Move the input closer to the base case
questions.explanation: Progress toward the base case ensures the recursion can terminate.

questions.prompt: What can happen when recursion continues too deeply?
options: The compiler changes the return type
questions.explanation: Each active call uses stack space, which is limited.

questions.prompt: When may an iterative solution be preferable?
questions.answer: When recursion depth could become very large
options: When recursion depth could become very large
When a method needs a parameter
When a program uses a String
When a class has a field
questions.explanation: A loop can avoid deep call-stack growth.
